subs.title: Locus and Problems with Other Conics

questions.q: Each of the four inequalities given below defines a region in the \(xy\) plane. One of these four regions does not have the following property. For any two points \((x_1,y_1)\) and \((x_2,y_2)\) in the region, the point \(\left(\dfrac{x_1+x_2}2,\dfrac{y_1+y_2}2\right)\) is also in the region. The inequality defining this region is
questions.sol: The property is convexity. \(x^2-y^2\ge1\) consists of two separate pieces: \((\pm1,0)\) belong to it but their mid point \((0,0)\) does not.

questions.q: The equation \(\dfrac{x^2}{1-r}-\dfrac{y^2}{1+r}=1\), \(|r|<1\) represents
questions.sol: For \(|r|<1\) both \(1-r\) and \(1+r\) are positive.

questions.q: If \(x=9\) is the chord of contact of the hyperbola \(x^2-y^2=9\) then the equation of the corresponding pair of tangents is
The curve described parametrically by \(x=t^2+t+1\), \(y=t^2-t+1\) represents
For hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{\cos^2\alpha}-\dfrac{y^2}{\sin^2\alpha}=1\) which of the following remains constant with change in '\(\alpha\)'
questions.sol: \(a^2e^2=a^2+b^2=\cos^2\alpha+\sin^2\alpha=1\): the foci are always \((\pm1,0)\).

questions.q: If the line \(2x+\sqrt6y=2\) touches the hyperbola \(x^2-2y^2=4\), then the point of contact is
questions.sol: Tangent at \((x_0,y_0)\): \(xx_0-2yy_0=4\). Compare with \(4x+2\sqrt6y=4\).

questions.q: A hyperbola, having the transverse axis of length \(2\sin\theta\), is confocal with the ellipse \(3x^2+4y^2=12\). Then its equation is
questions.sol: Ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}4+\dfrac{y^2}3=1\) has foci \((\pm1,0)\). Hyperbola: \(a=\sin\theta\), \(b^2=1-\sin^2\theta\).

questions.q: Consider a branch of the hyperbola \(x^2-2y^2-2\sqrt2x-4\sqrt2y-6=0\) with vertex at the point \(A\). Let \(B\) be one of the end points of its latus rectum. If \(C\) is the focus of the hyperbola nearest to the point \(A\), then the area of the triangle \(ABC\) is
Let \(P(6,3)\) be a point on the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\). If the normal at the point \(P\) intersects the \(x\)-axis at \((9,0)\) then the eccentricity of the hyperbola is
questions.sol: Normal: \(\dfrac{a^2x}6+\dfrac{b^2y}3=a^2+b^2\) meets the axis at \(x=6e^2=9\).

questions.q: The equation \(2x^2+3y^2-8x-18y+35=k\) represents
If the circle \(x^2+y^2=a^2\) intersects the hyperbola \(xy=c^2\) in four points \(P(x_1,y_1)\), \(Q(x_2,y_2)\), \(R(x_3,y_3)\), \(S(x_4,y_4)\) then
questions.sol: Eliminating \(y\): \(x^4-a^2x^2+c^4=0\) (no \(x^3\) term, constant \(c^4\)); the same equation holds for \(y\).

questions.q: Let a hyperbola pass through the focus of the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\). The transverse and conjugate axes of this hyperbola coincide with the major and minor axes of the given ellipse, also the product of eccentricities of given ellipse and hyperbola is \(1\), then
questions.sol: Ellipse: \(e=\dfrac35\), focus \((3,0)\). Hyperbola: \(a=3\), \(e'=\dfrac53\), \(b^2=9\left(\dfrac{25}9-1\right)=16\), focus \((ae',0)=(5,0)\).

questions.q: An ellipse intersects the hyperbola \(2x^2-2y^2=1\) orthogonally. The eccentricity of the ellipse is reciprocal of that of the hyperbola. If the axes of the ellipse are along the coordinate axes, then
questions.sol: The hyperbola has \(e=\sqrt2\) and foci \((\pm1,0)\). Orthogonal central conics are confocal, so the ellipse has \(ae=1\) with \(e=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\): \(a^2=2\), \(b^2=1\).

questions.q: Let the eccentricity of the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\) be reciprocal to that of the ellipse \(x^2+4y^2=4\). If the hyperbola passes through a focus of the ellipse, then
opts: the equation of the hyperbola is \(\dfrac{x^2}3-\dfrac{y^2}2=1\)
a focus of the hyperbola is \((2,0)\)
the eccentricity of the hyperbola is \(\sqrt{\dfrac53}\)
the equation of the hyperbola is \(x^2-3y^2=3\)
questions.sol: Ellipse: \(e=\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\), focus \((\sqrt3,0)\). Hyperbola: \(e=\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\), \(a^2=3\), \(b^2=3\left(\dfrac43-1\right)=1\), focus \((ae,0)=(2,0)\).

questions.q: Tangents are drawn to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}4=1\), parallel to the straight line \(2x-y=1\). The points of contact of the tangents on the hyperbola are
questions.sol: Slope \(\dfrac{4x}{9y}=2\) gives \(x=\dfrac{9y}2\); then \(\dfrac{9y^2}4-\dfrac{y^2}4=1\), \(y=\pm\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\).

questions.q: Consider the hyperbola \(H:x^2-y^2=1\) and a circle \(S\) with center \(N(x_2,0)\). Suppose that \(H\) and \(S\) touch each other at a point \(P(x_1,y_1)\) with \(x_1>1\) and \(y_1>0\). The common tangent to \(H\) and \(S\) at \(P\) intersects the \(x\)-axis at point \(M\). If \((l,m)\) is the centroid of the triangle \(PMN\), then the correct expression(s) is(are)
questions.sol: Tangent \(xx_1-yy_1=1\): \(M=\left(\dfrac1{x_1},0\right)\). The normal \(\dfrac x{x_1}+\dfrac y{y_1}=2\) passes through \(N\): \(x_2=2x_1\). So \(l=x_1+\dfrac1{3x_1}\) and \(m=\dfrac{y_1}3=\dfrac{\sqrt{x_1^2-1}}3\).

questions.q: If \(2x-y+1=0\) is a tangent to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\), then which of the following cannot be sides of a right angled triangle?

Let \(a\) and \(b\) be positive real numbers such that \(a>1\) and \(b<a\). Let \(P\) be a point in the first quadrant that lies on the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\). Suppose the tangent to the hyperbola at \(P\) passes through the point \((1,0)\), and suppose the normal to the hyperbola at \(P\) cuts off equal intercepts on the coordinate axes. Let \(\Delta\) denote the area of the triangle formed by the tangent at \(P\), the normal at \(P\) and the \(x\)-axis. If \(e\) denotes the eccentricity of the hyperbola, then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.sol: Tangent through \((1,0)\): \(x_0=a^2\). Normal slope \(-1\), so tangent slope \(\dfrac{b^2x_0}{a^2y_0}=1\): \(y_0=b^2\). On the curve: \(a^2-b^2=1\), so \(e^2=2-\dfrac1{a^2}\in(1,2)\). The normal meets the axis at \((a^2+b^2,0)\): \(\Delta=\dfrac12(a^2+b^2-1)b^2=b^4\).

questions.q: For any real \(t\), \(x=\dfrac{e^t+e^{-t}}2\), \(y=\dfrac{e^t-e^{-t}}2\) is a point on the hyperbola \(x^2-y^2=1\). Find the area bounded by this hyperbola and the lines joining its centre to the points corresponding to \(t_1\) and \(-t_1\).
questions.sol: Area \(=2\left[\dfrac12x_1y_1-\displaystyle\int_1^{x_1}y\,dx\right]\). With \(x=\cosh t\): \(\displaystyle\int_0^{t_1}\sinh^2t\,dt=\dfrac{\sinh2t_1}4-\dfrac{t_1}2\) and \(\dfrac12x_1y_1=\dfrac{\sinh2t_1}4\). So the area is \(t_1\).

questions.q: The angle between a pair of tangents drawn from a point \(P\) to the parabola \(y^2=4ax\) is \(45^\circ\). Show that the locus of the point \(P\) is a hyperbola.
questions.sol: For \(P(h,k)\): \(m^2h-mk+a=0\). \(\tan45^\circ=\dfrac{|m_1-m_2|}{1+m_1m_2}\) gives \(\left(1+\dfrac ah\right)^2=\dfrac{k^2}{h^2}-\dfrac{4a}h\), i.e. \((h+3a)^2-k^2=8a^2\).

questions.q: Tangents are drawn to the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) from any point on the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}4=1\). Find the locus of the midpoint of the chord of contact.
questions.sol: From \((3\sec\theta,2\tan\theta)\) the chord of contact is \(3x\sec\theta+2y\tan\theta=9\); with mid point \((h,k)\) it is \(hx+ky=h^2+k^2\). Comparing: \(\sec\theta=\dfrac{3h}{h^2+k^2}\), \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{9k}{2(h^2+k^2)}\); use \(\sec^2\theta-\tan^2\theta=1\).

questions.q: An ellipse has eccentricity \(\dfrac12\) and one focus at the point \(P\left(\dfrac12,1\right)\). Its one directrix is the common tangent, nearer to the point \(P\), to the circle \(x^2+y^2=1\) and the hyperbola \(x^2-y^2=1\). Then the equation of the ellipse in the standard form is ........
questions.sol: The common tangents are \(x=\pm1\); the nearer one is \(x=1\). \(\left(x-\dfrac12\right)^2+(y-1)^2=\dfrac14(x-1)^2\) gives \(3\left(x-\dfrac13\right)^2+4(y-1)^2=\dfrac13\).

questions.q:
Match the statements in Column I with the properties in Column II.
Column IColumn II
(i) Two intersecting circles(A) have a common tangent
(ii) Two mutually external circles(B) have a common normal
(iii) Two circles, one strictly inside the other(C) do not have a common tangent
(iv) Two branches of a hyperbola(D) do not have a common normal
questions.sol: The line of centres is a common normal of any two circles, and the transverse axis is a common normal of the two branches. Intersecting or external circles have common tangents; a circle strictly inside another has none, and no line touches both branches of a hyperbola.

questions.q:
Let \(H:\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), where \(a>b>0\), be a hyperbola in the \(xy\)-plane whose conjugate axis \(LM\) subtends an angle of \(60^\circ\) at one of its vertices \(N\). Let the area of the triangle \(LMN\) be \(4\sqrt3\).
List-IList-II
P. The length of the conjugate axis of \(H\) is1. \(8\)
Q. The eccentricity of \(H\) is2. \(\dfrac4{\sqrt3}\)
R. The distance between the foci of \(H\) is3. \(\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\)
S. The length of the latus rectum of \(H\) is4. \(4\)
The correct option is:
questions.sol: \(\tan30^\circ=\dfrac ba\) and area \(ab=4\sqrt3\): \(b=2\), \(a=2\sqrt3\). Conjugate axis \(4\); \(e=\sqrt{1+\dfrac4{12}}=\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\); \(2ae=8\); latus rectum \(\dfrac{2b^2}a=\dfrac4{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
The circle \(x^2+y^2-8x=0\) and hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) intersect at the points \(A\) and \(B\).
Equation of a common tangent with positive slope to the circle as well as to the hyperbola is
questions.sol: For \(2x-\sqrt5y+4=0\): \(m=\dfrac2{\sqrt5}\), \(c=\dfrac4{\sqrt5}\) and \(c^2=9m^2-4=\dfrac{16}5\) ✓; its distance from the centre \((4,0)\) is \(\dfrac{12}3=4\), the radius ✓.

questions.q:
Comprehension
The circle \(x^2+y^2-8x=0\) and hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}4=1\) intersect at the points \(A\) and \(B\).
Equation of the circle with \(AB\) as its diameter is
questions.sol: Putting \(y^2=8x-x^2\) in the hyperbola: \(13x^2-72x-36=0\), \(x=6\) (the other root is negative). \(A,B=(6,\pm2\sqrt3)\): \((x-6)^2+y^2=12\).

questions.q: The line \(2x+y=1\) is tangent to the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\). If this line passes through the point of intersection of the nearest directrix and the \(x\)-axis, then the eccentricity of the hyperbola is _____.
questions.sol: Through \(\left(\dfrac ae,0\right)\): \(a=\dfrac e2\). Tangency: \(1=4a^2-b^2=a^2(5-e^2)=\dfrac{e^2(5-e^2)}4\), so \(e^4-5e^2+4=0\) and \(e=2\).

questions.q: Consider the hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{100}-\dfrac{y^2}{64}=1\) with foci at \(S\) and \(S_1\), where \(S\) lies on the positive \(x\)-axis. Let \(P\) be a point on the hyperbola, in the first quadrant. Let \(\angle SPS_1=\alpha\), with \(\alpha<\dfrac\pi2\). The straight line passing through the point \(S\) and having the same slope as that of the tangent at \(P\) to the hyperbola, intersects the straight line \(S_1P\) at \(P_1\). Let \(\delta\) be the distance of \(P\) from the straight line \(SP_1\), and \(\beta=S_1P\). Then the greatest integer less than or equal to \(\dfrac{\beta\delta}9\sin\dfrac\alpha2\) is _____.
questions.sol: The tangent at \(P\) bisects \(\angle SPS_1\) and \(SP_1\) is parallel to it, so \(\delta=SP\sin\dfrac\alpha2\). In \(\Delta SPS_1\): \(4a^2e^2=(S_1P-SP)^2+4\,S_1P\cdot SP\sin^2\dfrac\alpha2\), so \(S_1P\cdot SP\sin^2\dfrac\alpha2=a^2e^2-a^2=b^2=64\). \(\left[\dfrac{64}9\right]=7\).

questions.q:
Let \(S\) denote the locus of the point of intersection of the pair of lines \(4x-3y=12\alpha\), \(4\alpha x+3\alpha y=12\), where \(\alpha\) varies over the set of non-zero real numbers. Let \(T\) be the tangent to \(S\) passing through the points \((p,0)\) and \((0,q)\), \(q>0\), and parallel to the line \(4x-\dfrac3{\sqrt2}y=0\).
Then the value of \(pq\) is
questions.sol: Multiplying the equations: \(16x^2-9y^2=144\), i.e. \(\dfrac{x^2}9-\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\). Tangent of slope \(m=\dfrac{4\sqrt2}3\): \(y=mx\pm\sqrt{9m^2-16}=mx\pm4\). So \(q=4\), \(p=-\dfrac4m=-\dfrac3{\sqrt2}\).

questions.q:
Consider the ellipse \(E\) given by \(\dfrac{x^2}{18}+\dfrac{y^2}{12}=1\). Let \(H\) be the hyperbola whose eccentricity is the reciprocal of the eccentricity of \(E\) and whose foci are the same as that of \(E\). Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be the points of intersection of \(H\) and the parabola \(\sqrt5y=x^2\) in the first quadrant. Let \(d\) be the distance between \(P\) and \(Q\).
If \(a\) and \(b\) are the integers such that \(d^2=a+b\sqrt5\), then the value of \(a-b\) is ______.
